title: Case study: Kallio & Lehtonen Kiinteistöt, shared mailbox triage

blocks.text: First response time in a 4,800-apartment property manager's shared inbox fell from a measured median of 26 h to 7.5 h in a two-week pilot

rows: Category accuracy of classifier vs. staff labels
3 cases last quarter (per Laura, not verified)
2 of 3 (3rd prefers own way, pair session planned)

blocks.text: The shared inbox isannointi@ receives around 140 mails a day, and faults, water damage, sauna bookings and payment questions all land in the same place. The assistants triage every mail by hand. The problem as the team described it: urgent items can wait more than a working day, and the team is busy with the sorting itself.

Velho built the smallest useful version: a classifier that labels each incoming mail into one of six categories with an urgency flag, and drafts a suggested reply inside the Outlook shared mailbox. Nothing is sent automatically. Urgent mails trigger an SMS to the on-call person, with a keyword fallback if the model is unavailable. Tone was tuned after the first feedback round, using examples from the team's own sent mails.

Two assistants piloted the tool in weeks 3 and 4. Two of the three assistants use it daily; the third works their own way, and a pair session is planned. The team also added a banner asking reviewers to check apartment numbers and other fields, after a spot check of 20 drafts found 2 with the wrong apartment number.

In the two-week pilot, median first response time dropped from 26 h to 7.5 h. The assistants believe triage time roughly halved, but this was not timed. The result is promising but early: a two-week pilot with two users, and the triage-time claim still needs measurement.

blocks.label: LinkedIn post
blocks.text:
A mailbox that got 140 mails a day, and a median first response of 26 hours.

For a property manager with 4,800 apartments, the shared inbox was where faults, water damage and payment questions all waited in one queue.

We built a small classifier for them: six categories, an urgency flag that texts the on-call person, and a suggested reply in Outlook. Nothing sends itself. The assistants still read every draft.

In a two-week pilot with two assistants, median first response went from 26 h to 7.5 h. It's early, and the sample is small, but it's a start.

If your team lives in a shared inbox, we'd like to hear how you triage it.

blocks.label: One-pager summary
blocks.text:
Client: Kallio & Lehtonen Kiinteistöt Oy (property management, ~4,800 apartments)
Problem: shared inbox of ~140 mails/day mixing faults, water damage, sauna and payment queries; manual triage; median first response 26 h
Built: LLM classifier (6 categories + urgency flag), suggested reply drafts in Outlook shared mailbox, SMS alert for urgent mails, no auto-send
Validation: 88% category accuracy and 94% urgent recall on 400 historic mails
Pilot result: median first response 26 h to 7.5 h over two weeks with two assistants
Status: two of three assistants using daily; GDPR: DPA signed, EU-only tenant data, 30-day logs
